title: Open Quantum Launches Native Qrisp Integration for High-Level QPU Execution Across IonQ, Rigetti, IQM, and AQT Hardware - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Open Quantum (Quantum Rings with qBitTensor Labs) released a native plugin for the Eclipse Foundation's open-source Qrisp language that compiles high-level Qrisp programs and runs them on IonQ, Rigetti, IQM and AQT QPUs without vendor-specific gate-level code. The SDK translates Qrisp into Qiskit circuits, validates them against each QPU's gate set and coupling map, and submits via OpenQASM, enabling single-string backend switching across trapped-ion and superconducting hardware.

insights.claim: Open Quantum, a quantum execution platform developed by Quantum Rings with qBitTensor Labs, released a native plugin letting developers compile and run high-level Qrisp programs directly on QPUs from IonQ, Rigetti, IQM and AQT without writing vendor-specific gate-level code or changing algorithm logic.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Software abstraction layers that span vendors reduce lock-in and could commoditize access to individual QPU providers.
insights.quote: without writing vendor-specific gate-level code or altering algorithm logic

insights.claim: The Open Quantum Qrisp plugin offers single-string backend switching between trapped-ion and superconducting quantum architectures by hooking into Qrisp's native execution routines.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Easy switching between modalities lets users benchmark and route workloads to whichever hardware performs best, intensifying vendor competition.
insights.quote: providing single-string backend switching across both trapped-ion and superconducting architectures

insights.claim: Unlike traditional quantum SDKs that require manually wiring physical qubits, applying gates and managing uncomputation of ancillary qubits, Qrisp provides typed quantum variables, automated qubit allocation, memory management and built-in quantum arithmetic.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Higher-level abstractions lower the skill barrier for quantum development, potentially widening the developer base and demand for QPU time.
insights.quote: Qrisp introduces software-engineering abstractions to quantum computing
insights.locator: Traditional quantum development SDKs require engineers

themes.theme: Compilation pipeline via Qiskit and OpenQASM

insights.claim: The Open Quantum SDK compiles Qrisp data structures into intermediate Qiskit circuits, flattens multi-register variables, validates against the target QPU's basis gate set and coupling map, submits jobs via OpenQASM, and decodes measurement counts back into Qrisp data types.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Reliance on Qiskit and OpenQASM as intermediate layers reinforces them as de facto industry interoperability standards.

insights.claim: Hardware targets supported by the Open Quantum Qrisp integration include IonQ Forte-1 (trapped ion, 36 qubits, 99.6% two-qubit gate fidelity) and Rigetti Cepheus-1 (superconducting, 108 qubits, 99.1% CZ gate fidelity, modular chiplet).
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Side-by-side specs show the trade-off between higher qubit count (Rigetti) and higher gate fidelity (IonQ) among listed public vendors.
insights.locator: Supported QPU Hardware Targets via Open Quantum Qrisp Integration

insights.claim: Other supported targets are IQM Emerald (superconducting, 54 qubits, 99.5% CZ fidelity, European HPC integration), IQM Garnet (superconducting, 20 qubits, 99.5% CZ fidelity) and AQT Ibex-Q1 (trapped ion, 12 qubits, fully connected, room-temperature rack).
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: European hardware vendors IQM and AQT gain reach through the same cross-vendor software channel as US players.
insights.locator: Supported QPU Hardware Targets via Open Quantum Qrisp Integration

themes.theme: Qrisp ecosystem and European open-source push

insights.claim: The Open Quantum integration extends Qrisp's existing CUDA-Q integration, builds on Qrisp 0.8's Shor's algorithm compilation benchmarks, and supports European open-source goals under the Horizon Europe Q-VERSE consortium.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Public European funding behind open-source quantum software signals policy support for a sovereign, vendor-neutral quantum stack.
insights.quote: supports broader European open-source software goals under the Horizon Europe Q-VERSE consortium
